# FG-INT-0010

| 項目 | 値 |
|---|---|
| HTTP ステータス | 400 |
| 重大度 | warn |
| Runbook | [`webhook-delivery`](../../ops/runbooks/webhook-delivery.md) |
| 発生させるテスト | `loopback_target_is_int_0010` |

## 利用者向けメッセージ

- ja: この送り先は許可されていません。
- en: This destination is not allowed.
- id: Tujuan ini tidak diizinkan.

## 原因 (cause)

A webhook URL or delivery was refused before anything was sent (ADR-0016 §8: only the operator's allowlist; SSRF defences resolved at connect time). On a create or update (400): the URL is not an absolute http(s) URL of at most 2048 bytes (`invalid_url`), uses http while `webhook.allow_http` is false (`scheme`), carries user information (`userinfo`) or a fragment (`fragment`), names a host and port that `webhook.allowed_targets` does not list (`not_allowlisted`; the list is empty by default, so nothing can be delivered until the operator adds the internal receivers), or names an address that is always refused whatever the list says (`loopback`, `link_local` — 169.254.169.254 metadata included —, `unspecified`, `multicast`, `broadcast`, `reserved`, `ipv4_compatible`, `nat64`, `six_to_four`; an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address is judged by its IPv4). At delivery time the same checks run again on the addresses the name resolves to now, and the connection is pinned to the checked address (DNS rebinding): `resolved_denied` when any resolved address is in an always-refused range, `resolved_not_allowlisted`, `dns` when the name does not resolve. A delivery is also refused when the webhook's owner (the person who created it) can no longer manage webhooks of the project (`owner_lost`: membership removed, demoted below Maintainer, account disabled, project pending deletion). The user sees only the one sentence; the reason is in the log.

## 調べ方 (diagnosis)

The log event carries `reason`, `origin` (scheme://host:port, never the path, query or user information) and, at delivery time, `webhook_id`, `delivery_id` and `address` (the resolved address that was refused); for `owner_lost` `owner_id` and `decision` (the code authorize() answered). Compare with the server's `webhook.allowed_targets` (`forge doctor` prints `webhook.allowed_targets`) and with `nslookup <host>` on the server.

## 対処 (fix)

If the receiver is a legitimate internal system, the operator adds `host:port` (or `cidr:port`) to `webhook.allowed_targets` and restarts (runbook webhook-delivery); never allowlist loopback, link-local or metadata addresses (they are refused regardless). For `owner_lost`, a Maintainer recreates the webhook under their own name, or the owner's role is restored.
